blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 73 in June to 79 in October (+8.2%), and it took 11.5% of the city’s 287 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 294 in June to 236 in October (−19.7%), and it took 51.4% of the city’s 407 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Central Abbotsford for detached houses in September (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in June, August, October (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in September (a sellers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Central Abbotsford
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple infill parcels are the default land form: The central area mixes older single detached streets (RS3, RS5 and infill RS3-i / RS7 zones) with the city's deepest strata stock. A vacant or teardown parcel on those streets is a fee-simple lot: the buyer's own title, no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fee — zoning, the two neighbourhood plans and any registered covenants govern what can replace the existing house.

Lot character: RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m²; RS5 minimum interior lot 420 m²; and RS7 (Infill Residential Zone) minimum lot size 300 m² for new interior lots, with minimum lot width 10.0 m and depth 22.5 m — among the smallest detached lot minimums in the city. RS3-i (Urban Residential Zone, Infill) is named in City council material for Maple Street in the Historic Downtown plan area.

: a September 16, 2025 City council report (PDS 172-2025) processes a rezoning of 2330 Fir Street (Lots 30 and 31) from RS3-i to RS7 to facilitate a three-lot subdivision, consistent with the Urban 3 – Infill designation — with the standard conditions in that report being a development agreement / cash-in-lieu for road and utility upgrades under the Development Bylaw, a Community Amenity Contribution, a s.219 covenant limiting density on the new lots, and resolution of unbudgeted funding items. That report is documented here as the area's subdivision PROCESS in action — a rezoning-led, condition-heavy route to three lots — not as for-sale inventory: the Fir Street lots are not a named development and no lot is offered here.

The Rail District is a development site / land assembly, documented as such — never as lot inventory: Nineteen acres of assembled downtown land is the core's real "land" story — but it is a developer's master-plan site selling homes, and no source checked offers individual lots in it. Do not present Rail District ground as buyable lots.

Bare-land strata: none verified in this sub-area: A bare-land strata lot, wherever it exists, is strata tenure: Form B, strata fees and bylaws apply to the lot. Any "bare-land strata" claim for a central address is not confirmed until a strata plan is produced.
Built-form developments — NOT land: They confirm the core builds UP on its land; none sells lots.
: The core's presales (Rail District phases, Mahogany) sell homes. No lot presale was verified on any developer or City source.
ALR vs non-ALR split: A buyer told a central lot is ALR should treat the claim itself as not confirmed until the ALC map is read.
Servicing: Servicing cost for a specific development site: Not confirmed until its Works and Services Report is read.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Central Abbotsford

items.t: The City's own commercial study describes the City Centre as a roughly rectangular area bordered approximately by Peardonville Road and Mill Lake to the south; Ware Street, Mill Lake Road and Horn Street to the east; Parkview Street and Tims Street to the west; and to the north by a line roughly parallel to George Ferguson Way and Maclure Road, centred on South Fraser Way. The Historic Downtown plan's focused redevelopment area is bounded in plan material by Pine Street, Cyril Street, McDougall Avenue and McCallum Road.

Where land actually trades: there is no greenfield ground in the core. Land changes hands as (1) individual infill / teardown parcels on the older detached streets, (2) small subdivisions carved out of those streets through rezoning, and (3) development sites assembled for the plan-designated multi-family forms — the Rail District being the named example.

Schools physically in the central area (SD34 sites): Godson Elementary (33130 Bevan Ave), Dormick Park Elementary (32161 Dormick Avenue), Abbotsford Middle and Abbotsford Senior Secondary. Two settled locator chains are carried in.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Central Abbotsford

items.t: Zoning: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 governs: The land-relevant central zones as the research states them: RS3 (minimum interior lot 540 m²), RS5 (420 m²), RS7 Infill (300 m² minimum, 10.0 m width, 22.5 m depth) and RS3-i infill. In the core, the zone plus the neighbourhood-plan designation — not the street's current houses — decides a parcel's real value.

Plans: two neighbourhood plans inside Abbotsforward 2050: The City Centre Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2913-2019) and the Historic Downtown Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2920-2019) are the adopted plans for the core, under Abbotsforward 2050 — Abbotsford's CURRENT Official Community Plan, adopted December 2025. Historic Downtown designations that price land: Urban 1 – Midrise (up to 6 storeys), Urban Centre – Mixed Use, Urban 2 – Ground Oriented (rowhouses, townhouse, multiplex or duplex housing) and Urban 3 – Infill (single detached with some ground-oriented duplexes). Abbotsforward 2050 also states a new mixed-use centre between the hospital and Mill Lake Park and a Primary Transit Corridor along South Fraser Way between Clearbrook and McCallum Road.

SSMUH / added units on a lot: the bylaw's s.140 small-scale multi-unit provision allows 3 units on lots 280 m² or less and 4 units on lots greater than 280 m² in the stated conditions, and s.140.3.8 permits one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings. Abbotsford's suite cap is under 50% of the principal dwelling, and a coach/garden suite is capped at 15% of lot area to a maximum of 100 m² — Abbotsford's rules ONLY (standing corrections, commissioning brief, Nov 1, 2026). This 3–4-unit provision is the core's main lot-value lever: a teardown parcel's price is routinely its unit count, so the s.140 conditions must be read for the specific lot before paying for potential.

Flood / watercourse diligence: Willband Creek runs through the Historic Downtown / central area and is named in City Historic Downtown plan material. The central upland is not Sumas Prairie — but parcel-level floodplain status still requires a City floodplain map check for any lot near the creek, and no lot should be priced as flood-free on the neighbourhood name alone.

Heritage diligence: the Gur Sikh Temple (Abbotsford Sikh Temple) at 33089 South Fraser Way is a designated National Historic Site in the core — a reminder that Historic Downtown parcels can carry heritage and design expectations under the neighbourhood plan even where no single-lot heritage designation is documented. Parcel-level heritage status: Not confirmed until the plan schedules and title are read for the lot.

ALR rules — stated for completeness, with their local weight: subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; Strata Property Act s.239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s.21(1)); ALC residence caps are a principal residence of 500 m² or less, a suite only within the principal residence, and an additional residence of 90 m² (40 ha or less) / 186 m² (over 40 ha). No ALR parcel is documented in this sub-area, so these rules are carried here only so a mislabelled listing can be tested against them — they are not the core's governing frame.

Farm class (BC Assessment) — the full three-tier form, for any farm-claimed parcel: $2,500 of farm income on a farm operation of 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value in excess of 4 ha on operations over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — B.C. Reg. 411/95, s.5, applications by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" statement is an ERROR and is not asserted here.

If a lot were bare-land strata (no verified case in the core): the BC strata block would apply to the LOT — Form B diligence (fee, approved levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 plus up to 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions).

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Abbotsford

items.t: The core's smallest-lot zone is also its rezoning story. Small-lot does not automatically mean maximum-density: read the covenants registered on the new titles.

The Rail District's 19 acres are the exception that proves the core's rule. One developer assembling 19 acres in Historic Downtown is newsworthy precisely because central land otherwise trades parcel by parcel. The assembly sells townhomes and apartments (The Abby Townhome Series, The Mason) — a land buyer cannot buy into it lot by lot.
The growth arrow in the current plan points at a gap, not a field. Parcels on that seam carry plan value that their current houses do not show.
The honest zero in is the research position, not a research failure.

A "Central Abbotsford" land label in a feed may not be central at all. The King Road cluster (34248 King Road) is filed under Central Abbotsford, Poplar and Abbotsford East by different feeds for the same address; the sub-area label follows the feed, not the ground. For land diligence the PID, the zone and the plan designation are the stable identifiers.

blocks.text: Mobile and manufactured homes in Central Abbotsford
Verified park inside Central Abbotsford: 1 — Georgian Park, pad rental.
The parks and communities

items.t: Georgian Park: Plainly: a home here sits on a rented pad — the buyer owns the home (a chattel) and rents the pad; the buyer does not own the land. The tenancy is governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, not the Strata Property Act.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Central Abbotsford

items.t: The City plans covering the core are the City Centre Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2913-2019) and the Historic Downtown Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2920-2019).
The Historic Downtown plan's focused redevelopment area is bounded in plan material by Pine Street, Cyril Street, McDougall Avenue and McCallum Road.
Nearby areas: Abbotsford West to the west, Abbotsford East to the east, Poplar to the northwest.

Main roads named in City plan material: South Fraser Way (the commercial backbone), George Ferguson Way, McCallum Road, Clearbrook Road, Ware Street and Old Yale Road, with Highway 1 interchanges at McCallum Road and Clearbrook Road serving the central area.

Where the mobile-home stock in this sub-area sits: the one verified park, Georgian Park, is on Horn Street at the east edge of the City Centre frame above — Horn Street is named in that frame as an east-edge street.

Transit: Bourquin Exchange is in the central area; BC Transit Central Fraser Valley routes named in service material include 1 (Highstreet/UFV), 2 (Highstreet/McMillan), 4 (Saddle/Montrose), 5 (Clearbrook/Bourquin via Hospital), 12 (UFV/Bourquin), 17 (Industrial/Bourquin), 21 (Aldergrove/Abbotsford) and 31 (Abbotsford/Mission). No route serving the park address itself was verified — not confirmed at park level.

Schools physically in the central area, on SD34 school sites: Godson Elementary (33130 Bevan Ave), Dormick Park Elementary (32161 Dormick Avenue), Abbotsford Middle (33231 Bevan Avenue) and Abbotsford Senior Secondary (33355 Bevan Ave).

faq.a: Not from a subdivision or a lot release — none exists in the core. What you can buy is an individual infill or teardown parcel on the older detached streets (fee-simple), priced on its RS3/RS5/RS7 zoning and its plan designation, or — as a developer — assembled ground like the Rail District site, which is a master-plan land play, not lot inventory.
faq.q: Can I buy a bare lot in Central Abbotsford?

faq.a: RS7 (Infill Residential Zone) allows new interior lots down to 300 m², with minimum width 10.0 m and depth 22.5 m; RS3 minimum interior lot is 540 m² and RS5 is 420 m². But reaching RS7 usually takes a rezoning — the documented Fir Street route rezoned RS3-i to RS7 for a three-lot subdivision, with servicing, amenity and covenant conditions attached.
faq.q: How small can a new central lot be?

faq.a: Usually its unit potential: s.140 allows 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units on lots over 280 m² in the stated conditions, one secondary suite is permitted in all single detached dwellings (s.140.3.8), and the plan designations (Urban 2 – Ground Oriented; Urban 1 – Midrise to 6 storeys) set the larger forms. Confirm the zone section and designation for the parcel before paying for any of it — the SSMUH bylaw number in some material ("3560-2024") is not confirmed.
faq.q: What is an older central house actually worth as land?

faq.a: The servicing bill for a specific parcel is in its Works and Services Report: Not confirmed until that report is read.
faq.q: Is the parcel serviced, and who pays for upgrades?

faq.a: It turns on the seller and the parcel's history, per CRA GI-003: an individual's sale of personal-use land is generally exempt, but a sale in the course of a business or of a parcel created by subdividing into more than two parts can be taxable. A developer-sold newly created lot is the taxable pattern; a long-held family lot usually is not. Have the contract allocate the GST expressly.
faq.q: Do I pay GST on a teardown or a subdivided lot?

faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the park owns the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act. Plainly, a home on a rented pad is not land ownership.
faq.q: In Georgian Park, do I own the land?

faq.a: A park's age rule lives in its park rules and tenancy documents, not in a strata bylaw, so the written park rules are the deciding document; the Province's general park rule is that in a designated 55-plus park at least one tenant on the site must be 55 or older. Get the park's current rule in writing.
